functionalReqs: Real-time collaboration with many concurrent editors
hints: If two users insert at position 5 at the same time, how do both end up with the same text?
Compare Operational Transformation (central server orders ops) with CRDTs (ops commute). Which fits a server-centric design?

Route all editors of a document to one collaboration server (consistent hashing on doc ID), which sequences operations, transforms them, broadcasts over WebSocket, and appends to an op log; periodic snapshots for fast load; version history from snapshots plus ops.
nonFunctionalReqs: Edits appear for others within ~100–300 ms
No lost edits, including offline editing
problemStatement:
Design **Google Docs**: many users edit the same document at once and see each other's changes and cursors in real time.

Concurrent edits must converge to the same document on every screen without losing anyone's typing.

scaleHints.qps: Bursts of keystroke operations; ~100 editors on a hot document
scaleHints.storage: Documents plus operation logs and snapshots

title: Design Google Docs (Collaborative Editing)
